children: on Wednesday said its public-sector business has become its fastest-growing industry business at scale, with its defense business expanding 80% year over year as government agencies increase their use of artificial intelligence.
The software company said the update marks one year since it launched Missionforce, its platform for government that combines AI, data, applications, and cloud technology. Salesforce
said it now supports government operations in more than 30 countries, 60 U.S. federal agencies, all 15 Cabinet departments, all 50 states, and the six branches of the U.S. military.

The company highlighted several recent deployments and contracts, including a 10-year U.S. Army contract with a $5.6 billion ceiling to expand Missionforce National Security across the Army and Department of War.
The Army Human Resources Command selected the platform to provide AI-powered support to 9.2 million soldiers, veterans, civilian employees, and military families, Salesforce

The company also said the U.S. Air Force deployed Missionforce to modernize operations for a vehicle fleet valued at $13.5 billion, while the Transportation Security Administration is using an AI agent called Ace to handle about 100,000 traveler conversations a month. Salesforce
said Ace resolves 96% of routine inquiries without human escalation and has cut consumer-interaction costs by more than 90%.
also announced a collaboration with OpenAI
to bring advanced AI models and accelerated computing to Missionforce workloads and secure government environments.
The company said it was named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for National Civilian Government AI-Enabled Case Management.

title: Salesforce expands Missionforce across U.S. government agencies and military
